 Order

This Misc. Appeal and connected Civil Revisions have arisen out of common award passed on 31/05/2024 by 5th Additional Member Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Chhindwara deciding claim cases Nos. 101/2019, 102/2019 and 103/2019 respectively.

entities.text: 5th Additional Member Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Chhindwara
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: Appellant/Insurance Company in all the three cases is aggrieved of the finding of saddling it with the joint and several liberty to pay the compensation amount.

2. Brief facts of the cases are that claimant/respondent No.1 of all the three claim cases were travelling on a single motorcycle, which was being driven by claimant-Salman, when respondent No.2- Shubham dashed against their motorcycle, resulting into injuries to all three of them.

Compensation amount of Rs.15,00,000/-, Rs.15,00,000/- and Rs.1,00,00,000/- were claimed respectively in claim case Nos. 101/2019, 102/2019 and 103/2019 by respective claimants namely Ram Bahadur, Manmeet and Salman.

Learned Tribunal allowed their claim petitions by awarding Rs.64,093/-, Rs. 57,718 and Rs. 18,98,846/- in favour of respective respondent No.1/claimant by directing owner, driver and Insurance Company of the offending vehicle to pay this amount under their joint and several liability.
NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2026:MPHC-JBP:10652 3 MA-9283-2024 3.

Appellant/Insurance company is aggrieved of said finding and has placed emphasis on the fact that driving license of the respondent No.2 was forged and thus, he was driving the offending vehicle in violation of terms and conditions of the insurance policy.

Accordingly, a request has been made in M.A. 9283/2024 arisen out of claim case No.103/2019, Civil Revision No. 1138/2019 arisen out of claim case No.102/2019 and Civil Revision No. 1139/2019 arisen out of claim case No. 101/2019 to set aside the impugned award and exonerate the Insurance Company from liability to pay compensation amount.

4. Respondents No.1/claimants of all the three cases are contesting party here, while respondent Nos. 2 and 3, driver and owner of the offending vehicle, remained absent before this court, despite service of notice.

5. Appellant/Insurance Company had taken numerous grounds of defense before Tribunal, but before this Court, the only limited point pressed upon is that the respondent No.2 while driving the The New India Assurance Co Ltd. vs Salman Chauhan on 5 February, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/647365/
2 offending vehicle was not holding a valid and effective license and thus, there was a breach of condition of Insurance Policy.

entities.text: New India Assurance Co Ltd. vs Salman Chauhan
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
Accordingly, this Court has to decide only a limited issue and that is whether the appellant/Insurance Company was able to establish any breach of policy and if yes,
what should be the extent of its liability to pay compensation.

6. Appellant/Insurance Company examined its witness - Sandeep to prove the terms and conditions of the Insurance Policy marked as Ex. D/1, the investigator report marked as Ex. D/2 and the certificate issued by RTO, Nagpur, as Ex. D/3 confirming that no driving license was issued by that NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2026:MPHC-JBP:10652 4 MA-9283-2024 office in favour of respondent No.2.
The Tribunal did not believe his testimony for the reason that he was not authorized on behalf of Insurance Company to testify.
It is not clear what kind of authorization was being sought from this witness.
He was an employee of Insurance Company and definitely would have appeared before Tribunal for the testimony only upon the directions and authorization of his superior officer.
Law permits any competent witness, conversant with the facts of the case, to testify in Court and there is no need to obtain a letter of authorization for that purpose.

Further, if the Tribunal was not willing to give much credence to the testimony of this witness, wasn't it under an obligation to examine and appreciate the documents of exhibit D/1 and D/3.
7.

Tribunal was of the opinion that information Ex. D/3, received by investigator of insurance company from RTO, Nagpur, was to be proved only through the testimony of the responsible officer/employee of that office and no one from that office was examined by the Insurance Company, but whether the formal proof of Ex. D/3 was really required.
8.
Witness - Sandeep was examined to testify that driver-Shubham was not having a valid and effective driving license at the time of accident.
His testimony could have been easily rebutted by owner and driver of the vehicle by producing the valid driving license of respondent No.2.
Admittedly, driver did not appear in the witness box to face the drill of cross- examination.

Respondent No.3/owner of the offending vehicle namely Rukesh claimed in his testimony that the driver- Shubham was having a valid and effective driving license, which was seen by him before handing over NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2026:MPHC-JBP:10652 5 MA-9283-2024 offending vehicle for the purpose of driving.
Incidentally, said driving license was never placed by respondent No.3/owner on the record of Tribunal.
When cross examined on this point, he could not give any justification for withholding the said driving license.

9. In National Insurance Company Limited Vs. Swarn Singh and Others, 2004(3) SCC 297, the Apex Court held that, with a view of avoid the liability, Insurance Company must establish available defense and must also establish breach on the part of owner of the vehicle.

entities.text: National Insurance Company Limited Vs. Swarn Singh and Others, 2004(3) SCC 297
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The Apex Court was of the view that the burden of prove would be on the Insurance Company, however, it also added that no specific criteria could be laid down as to how said burden would be discharged, in as much as, it would depend on the facts and circumstances of each case.

In the present case, the driving license of respondent No.2-Shubham was not made available to the Insurance Company, therefore, even if we ignore the document of Ex. D/3, it can be deciphered that insurance company could have no idea when and from which office, the driving license of respondent No.2-Shubham was issued.

It has already been discussed that respondent No.3/owner, despite appearing in witness box, failed to The New India Assurance Co Ltd. vs Salman Chauhan on 5 February, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/647365/
3 produce even the photocopy of that driving license.

sentences.text:
10. In terms of these facts, learned counsel for the appellant has very aptly relied upon the decision of Hon'ble Apex court in the case of Pappu and others Vs. Vinod Kumar Lamba & Ors., 20018(1)
T.A.C. 360 (SC) , wherein the Apex Court has observed that if the driving license of the driver was not produced in support of the plea that offending vehicle was being plied by authorized person having a valid driving license, the Insurance Company NEUTRAL CITATION NO.
2026:MPHC-JBP:10652 6 MA-9283-2024 would become liable only after such foundational facts are pleaded and proved by the owner/driver of the offending vehicle.

entities.text:
Pappu and others Vs. Vinod Kumar Lamba & Ors., 20018(1)
T.A.C. 360 (SC)
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Thus, the primary liability to produce the original driving license or the photocopy thereof was on the owner/driver of the vehicle but they purposely withheld the document, if there was any, and the failure of their initial burden to prove the existence of a valid driving license, no burden of prove could have shifted on appellant/Insurance Company.

In support of this contention, learned counsel for the appellant has also placed reliance on the orders passed by this Court in the cases of The New India Assurance Company Ltd. Vs. Punnam Chandra Kesharwani @ Babu (M.A. No. 1373/2021 decided on 29.11.2023) , Branch Manager Oriental Insurance Company Ltd. Vs. Smt. Aarti & Ors.

entities.text: New India Assurance Company Ltd. Vs. Punnam Chandra Kesharwani @ Babu (M.A. No. 1373/2021
entities.label: PRECEDENT

entities.text: Branch Manager Oriental Insurance Company Ltd. Vs. Smt. Aarti & Ors
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
(M.A. No.
2206/2017 decided on 17.02.2024) and National Insurance Company Ltd. Vs. Bunti Bai & Ors.

entities.text: National Insurance Company Ltd. Vs. Bunti Bai & Ors
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
(M.A. No. 2075/2022 decided on 04/03/2024), wherein it was observed that the owner/driver of the offending vehicle is the best person under the provision of Section 106 of Indian Evidence Act,
having knowledge about the existence of a valid and effective driving license at the time of accident and if such an information is withheld, an adverse inference should be drawn against him.
11. Summing up the above discussion on facts and law, it is held that the offending vehicle was being driven at the time of accident in breach of insurance policy as the driving license of respondent No.2, which was never brought into the knowledge of Insurance Company nor was placed on record of Tribunal, was not in existence and therefore, it is held that the respondent No.2-Shubham was driving the offending vehicle without having any valid NEUTRAL CITATION NO.
2026:MPHC-JBP:10652 7 MA-9283-2024 and effective driving license on the date of accident and thus, a breach of policy was committed by respondent No.3/insured by allowing a person not having a valid driving license to drive the offending vehicle.

12. In terms of the decision of Hon'ble Apex Court in Swarn Singh (supra) and other cases cited above, on the question of liability of insurance company in such kind of breach, it is directed that appellant/Insurance Company, under the liability of pay and recover, shall, at the first instance,
satisfy the award and shall have the liberty to recover the compensation amount so paid from the owner of the offending vehicle i.e. respondent No.3.
13.
Accordingly, present appeal stands partly allowed in aforesaid terms.

14. Let a copy of this order along with records of the claim cases be sent back to the concerned Tribunal for information and necessary compliance.
(ANURADHA SHUKLA) JUDGE skt The New India Assurance Co Ltd. vs Salman Chauhan on 5 February, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/647365/
